failure_patterns.pattern: runtime_tool_import_error: Agents imported unavailable tool or cache modules instead of calling runtime-provided functions directly.

rejected_edits.content: - Execute every required search, filter, sort, or nearest-results action as a tool call, bind its exact return value to a local variable, and immediately save that same object with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. For a refinement, retrieve the exact listed compatible prior result, pass it as `prior_results` to the appropriate filter, and save the filter return under a new key; retrieval or a code comment alone does not perform the refinement. Use bound results for dependent calls. Do not use unlisted or invented cache keys, leave a result-producing call bare, or substitute hand-built data for tool results.
rejected_edits.target: - Bind the exact return value of every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call to a variable, then save it with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. Save refined results under a new key. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.

rejected_edits.content: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list or widen an exact value. For a one-sided minimum or maximum, use the documented scale endpoint for the unconstrained side (`[x, scale_max]` or `[scale_min, x]`). For hotel stars, whose range is 1–5, encode “at least x” as `[x, 5]` and “at most x” as `[1, x]`. Follow the schema’s actual scale for other bounds and do not guess undocumented endpoints.
rejected_edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
